title: Weather-adjusted seven-day flow-rank persistence had no clear change at 107 south-east Australian catchments in 2010-2021
abstract: We tested daily flow order apart from flow size in CAMELS-AUS v2.03. Within-year rank displacement is unchanged by a strictly increasing annual flow transformation. Historical weather fits used 1951-1996. In 107 mainland catchments, the 2010-2021 seven-day residual was +1.65% of reference displacement with AGCD rain and +0.02% with SILO rain. Conditional 95% shared-year and spatial-cell intervals were -10.04% to +11.66% and -9.98% to +9.46%. Neither gave a clear change. The two intervals did not both fit inside the planned ten-percent margin, so we do not claim unchanged persistence. Runoff stayed below the weather relation and zero-flow days rose. Complete-flow, few-zero and balanced-panel checks also gave seven-day intervals across zero. A synthetic control gave 25% lower mean flow and 10% faster log recession with identical ranks. Thus the null does not reject a drainage change. Limited weather skill, tied zeros, source error, 12 target years and selected gauges limit inference. Code, aggregate estimates, all draws, source hashes, figures and an independent audit are supplied. A fresh source rebuild reproduced all numerical estimates exactly. Raw and station-level data remain external.

display.caption: Weather-adjusted endpoints in 107 mainland catchments in 2010-2021. Seven-day rank displacement has no clear change, while runoff is lower and zero-flow days are more frequent. Bars are conditional 95% full-refit time and space intervals. Shading marks the planned ten-percent displacement margin. All outcomes use the same flow records.

Seven-day intervals cross zero in the model, block and sample checks. The historical target is 1982-1996. The balanced panel was added after the first estimates. Checks are dependent and their intervals are marginal.

A synthetic positive power transformation lowers mean flow by 25% and raises log recession by 10% while preserving every rank measure. Shuffling dates preserves the marginal flow values but changes displacement. This is a measurement control, not a physical catchment model.
